title: Create feed accepts URLs that sibling sync path rejects
reasoning: The bulk feed sync route validates every submitted URL and returns 422 for unsafe or malformed URLs before storing them, but the single-feed create route only checks for an existing row and then persists feed_data.url directly. That means POST /api/feeds can create active feed records with schemes, hostnames, or userinfo that the API already treats as invalid on the sibling creation path, leaving unusable feed configuration and inconsistent client behavior for the same FeedCreate/FeedSync-style inputs.
reproduction: POST /api/feeds with a body such as {"url":"file:///etc/passwd","title":"Bad","mode":"raw","is_active":true,"max_articles":5}. The create route reaches session.add/session.commit instead of returning the 422 used by /api/feeds/sync.
recommendation: Call validate_public_url(feed_data.url) at the start of create_feed, mapping ValueError to HTTP 422 with the same error shape used by sync_feeds. Apply the same validation before restoring a soft-deleted feed.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: test_create_feed only exercises a valid https URL and does not assert rejection of invalid, private, or non-http URLs.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that POST /api/feeds rejects a non-http URL or localhost/private-host URL with 422 and does not create a feed row.
minimumFixScope: app/api/feeds.py create_feed validation plus tests/test_feeds.py coverage for invalid create input.
